newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian RTS shares index rises to record close.
newsitem.headline: Russian RTS shares index rises to record close.

text.p: The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose 4.5 percent from last week's close to a record 262.34 on Monday, the NAUFOR brokers association said.
The previous high, set on January 13, was 251.49.
Turnover for the entire market was a robust $44.9 million, it said.
Dmitry Starenko, senior trader at Regent European Securities said investors were chasing each other into the market, which has been on a bull run since Christmas.
"The important thing is the direction of the money -- right now it is into Russia," he said.
Second tier shares showed the strongest growth for the day, following a slowdown in rises among leading shares.
Operators said investors had begun to look away from the most liquid stocks to find relatively undervalued bargains.
St Petersburg Telephone jumped to $1.38 at the close from $1.11 on Friday and Gazprom rose to $0.490 from $0.409.
LUKoil rose to $14.23 from $13.62, Norilsk Nickel to $6.28 from $5.95 and UES jumped to $0.1520 from $0.1385.
Sergei Kosynkin, head of equities at Bank Menatep, said that the market continued to rise as President Boris Yeltsin, in hospital with pneumonia but soon to be released, appeared to be improving.
"Doctors say Yeltsin is all right in hospital. Everyone is optimistic and neither doctors nor journalists are scaring us with bad news," he said.
